name: Shipping chokepoints
value: Hormuz mine strikes 26 Nov; Red Sea attacks
summary: Iran's Guards say two tankers hit Hormuz mines on 26 Nov; UKMTO reports blast off Dubai; Houthis hit Saudi Red Sea ports
state: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers hit mines north of Khasab on 26 Nov while using an unauthorised route through Hormuz (Deccan Herald, Reuters wire). UKMTO reported an explosion from an unknown projectile near a tanker 50 nautical miles west of Dubai on 26 Nov, with no damage or injuries (Times of Israel). In the Red Sea, the Houthis claimed attacks on Jeddah and Jazan ports on 25 Nov and a projectile hit Jazan port (Xinhua), so two chokepoints remain disrupted.
for_you: Expect continued delays and higher costs for goods shipped via the Gulf and Red Sea. Mariners should follow UKMTO and JMIC advisories.
rubric_hit: Hormuz materially impeded and Red Sea disrupted: two chokepoints at once

sources.title: Deccan Herald (Reuters) — Iran's Revolutionary Guards say two oil tankers hit sea mines near Oman's Khasab
Times of Israel — Projectile said to cause explosion near tanker west of Dubai
Xinhua — Houthis claim attacks on Saudi ports of Jeddah, Jazan; coalition says intercepted 8 drones

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
